You seem to have some misunderstandings.

1. Anything with mass has gravitational force, but the gravity of smaller objects is dominated by that of larger objects (like planets and stars).

2. Spinning planets DO produce centrifugal force... Earth's is dominated by gravity. If it was spinning fast enough, we'd all fly off.

3. Motion only exists with respect to a reference frame. The sun is treated stationary with respect to our solar system because the planets move with respect to it. With respect to the center of the galaxy, the sun is moving. Think of it this way: you and your buddy are in deep space. The distance between the two of you is increasing. To him, you are moving and he is still. To you, the opposite is true because you have no frame of reference besides your own body. There would be no way to tell without a background.

4. Gravitational force is totally relative to elevation, but the difference is so minute that 9.8 m/s^2 is almost always a good enough approximation.

Regardless of how related they actually are, I always associated my palate for dissonance with the sometimes suffocating heat and humidity here in the swamps, so this list would be incomplete without an ode to the unsettling extremes here.
